purpose: Test whether THR can describe one validator execution without turning validator success into a truth verdict or forcing new shared registry object types.

triggering_actor.boundary: Public GitHub account label from run metadata; not a THR living-person principal profile.

executed_checkout.basis: GitHub Actions checkout log for workflow run 35463860339
executed_checkout.boundary: The executed checkout is distinct from both the branch head that triggered the run and the PR's later current head.

declared_environment.boundary: Workflow declaration only; this fixture does not claim a complete hardware/OS/supply-chain reproduction environment.

observed_steps.name: Validate record, registry and view integrity

not_established: That the Human Record assertions checked by the validator are historically or factually true.
That the seven validator warnings are defects or harmless in every future use.
That GitHub Actions is an independent evidentiary witness to the underlying historical records.
That the declared workflow environment is fully reproducible from this fixture.
That the triggering GitHub account label identifies a living human beyond the public account context.
That successful execution grants GitHub, the triggering actor, or THR policy authority.
ceilings: CURRENT PR HEAD != HISTORICAL RUN HEAD
EXTERNAL SERVICE RECEIPT != INDEPENDENT CLAIM EVIDENCE
AUDIT OBSERVATION TIME != ORIGINAL RECEIPT CREATION TIME

metadata_reobservation.basis: Bounded Codex audit of fresh GitHub run/job metadata recorded on PR #52.
metadata_reobservation.boundary: This is the later audit observation time, not a reconstructed timestamp for creation of the original experimental receipt.
